record_scope_reconstruction: February7 2020 interruption of non-emergency Seaway bridge-system traffic arising on the North Channel/Cornwall Island approach. The protest location is within Canada; it affected the international system without occupying the US-bound South Channel span.

source_checks.finding: Full original locates protesters on North Bridge to Canadian Customs, quotes Cornwall police diversion at Brookdale/Water and tribal police emergency-only system closure; reports14:41–16:26.
February18 WWNY distinguishes the February7 Seaway event from a later Thousand Islands action and says there was no official tribal representation in the latter.

Indian Time reproduces council account: Akwesasne International Road occupation, walk over Cornwall bridge toward tollbooth, and reopening about16:30. This is not an exact match to the local14:41–16:26 clock.
Bridge operator January2014 announcement identifies the new low-level North Channel bridge, SIBC toll plaza and CBSA plaza; avoids substituting the demolished former high bridge.

Original OSM road bridge lies on the North Channel between Cornwall and Cornwall Island, separately from the southern international span and demolished high bridge. Current geometry is a reference, not a reconstruction of the 2020 toll-barrier footprint. Operator opening notice places the new low-level crossing in service in January2014.
